note: Volume I statements register: one row per formal statement. 'volume' names the volume the statement belongs to (I, II or III); exact placement is sorted out later (Sean Brady, 2026-10-30). Courtroom II fields are read from the case files by tools/statements_register.py. Rows with 'proposed_case' are the lead's proposals for work not yet done.

statements.statement: Matter displaces space, and that displacement accumulates.
statements.author: Sean Brady (2026-10-29)
statements.placement_note: Chapter II–III accumulation language points back to it

statements.statement: The farther you look out into space, the more accumulation you are looking through. (Not a challenge to Hubble's law; a different explanation of the same phenomena.)
statements.author: Sean Brady (2026-10-29)
statements.decider: Chapter XII differential test (q0 shift -6/pi under the readout) against distance data; distance duality g_L/g_A
statements.placement_note: Chapter XII §1 (road law) points to it

statements.statement: The Aquarium Thought Experiment (2023): a sealed full aquarium, a rock growing into existence, a halo, a pebble that slows and bends and leaves straight. Stands as envisioned.
statements.author: Sean Brady (2023; recorded 2026-10-29)
statements.placement_note: introduces A_0 (the water), A(r) (the halo as a 1/r potential), the ceiling (the full tank)

statements.statement: The three core objects: A_0 = 1/(12 pi) the floor; A(r) = r_s/r the lift; the ceiling 1/pi of the line of sight.
statements.author: Sean Brady (direction); Volume I Chapters II, III, XII
statements.decider: A_0 convention: source-only reading (floor drops out of the static exterior) adopted; the background-normalized reading rescales the lift by 1/(1-A_0)
statements.placement_note: Chapters II (floor), III (kernel), XII (road law) point to the definitions A_0 (the floor) already treated in Chapters II–III; concept note 1 defines it; no separate note needed (Sean Brady 2026-10-30).

statements.statement: The magic bell: a mirror clock near a supermassive black hole; a lone observer in a void with a bell that rings exactly when light strikes the mirror. Does the observer hear the bell and see the strike in unison? Not to be answered in the volume.
statements.author: Sean Brady (recorded 2026-10-29)
statements.decider: none by direction (the question stays open)
statements.placement_note: Chapter IV §39 (Epsilon+/Alpha+ rendering) points to Chapter I and carries Sean Brady's version

statements.statement: If A is not equal at two endpoints, accumulation must exist between them. (Converse fails: the Cassini conjunction.)
statements.author: Sean Brady (the result); Claude Code (the proof and the converse)
statements.decider: none needed (theorem); the converse's instance is the measured Cassini delay
statements.placement_note: Chapter IV §42–44 (finite logarithm, Cassini) supply the instance Sean Brady 2026-10-30: Chapter I introduces this conceptually (clock/road, GPS, Shapiro); full treatment in its own chapter.

statements.statement: Static exterior theorem (agreement): clock sqrt(1-a), radial ruler 1/sqrt(1-a), areal tangential ruler give Schwarzschild exactly; gamma = beta = 1; every static vacuum observable takes its GR value; Cassini measures the ruler declaration.
statements.author: web Claude (proposal); Claude Code (corrections); Sean Brady (framing)
statements.decider: kappa_s - 1 = gamma - 1 = (2.1 +- 2.3)e-5 (Cassini) as the test of the ruler declaration
statements.placement_note: replaces the benchmark language of Chapter IV §40 and §45 and Chapter V §3.3; Appendix A III.1–III.4 restated as 'declared, tested by Cassini, derivation open'

statements.statement: The departure: the static coordinate time to A = 1 is SAM's physical statement; the road ends at A = 1 (the astronaut runs out of road, not clock). Equal static numbers do not make equal theories.
statements.author: Sean Brady (2026-10-29); Chapter V
statements.decider: an observable distinguishing a road ending at A = 1 from an extended interior; none registered (Chapters V, XI)
statements.placement_note: Chapter V keeps the GR crossing as the comparison control

statements.statement: Between two endpoints SAM carries two numbers: the measurable distance L = int dl and the accumulation looked through Sigma = int a dl; the clock reads the endpoints, the road reads the path.
statements.author: Sean Brady (the split); Claude Code (the definitions)
statements.decider: a readout changing D_L and D_A by different factors (Chapter XII g_L/g_A); none registered
statements.placement_note: Chapter IV §40 (optical receiving law) points to it Sean Brady 2026-10-30: Chapter I introduces this conceptually (clock/road, GPS, Shapiro); full treatment in its own chapter.

statements.statement: GPS is the daily instance: the clock correction (endpoints, +38.6 us/day) and the road correction (path, picoseconds) come from one displacement and are applied separately.
statements.author: Sean Brady (the origin question); web Claude (the one-line closure); Claude Code (the numbers)
statements.decider: the operational figure 38.6 us/day and the eccentricity correction (proposed next case)
statements.placement_note: Chapter IV 'GPS comparison' points to Chapter I Sean Brady 2026-10-30: Chapter I introduces this conceptually (clock/road, GPS, Shapiro); full treatment in its own chapter.

statements.statement: The clock in motion: dtau/dt = sqrt(1-a) sqrt(1 - v_loc^2/c^2) exactly; tangential shorthand sqrt(1 - a - beta^2); circular orbits sqrt(1 - 3a/2); closure on the line a + beta^2 = 1 with light on it; escape v_loc^2 = a c^2.
statements.author: web Claude (the one line); Chapter IV (the exact law); Claude Code (corrections)
statements.placement_note: Chapter IV 'Motion requires a spatial metric' points to it Sean Brady 2026-10-30: Chapter I introduces this conceptually (clock/road, GPS, Shapiro); full treatment in its own chapter.

statements.statement: Velocity adds beta^2 to accumulation in the frame in which the field is static, not through the floor; the floor, having no gradient, defines no rest frame. Control: a floor-velocity term would put 66 ms/day into GPS clocks; it is absent.
statements.author: web Claude (the caveat); Claude Code (the numbers)
statements.decider: a quantitative bound on any floor-frame velocity term from GPS and optical-clock timing (proposed next case)
statements.placement_note: Appendix A II.3 (preferred-frame tests) restated with the GPS control

statements.statement: The spatial coefficient kappa_s is closed by a declared ruler reading (1/sqrt(1-a)), tested by Cassini, not derived; the retained road operator already fixes it at first order.
statements.author: Claude Code (correction to the proposal); Chapter IV
statements.note: 01_METRIC_THEOREM_20261029.md (What the theorem is, and is not)
statements.decider: a spatial coefficient derived from the retained source action would be the derivation (Appendix A interface)

statements.statement: A floor-frame velocity term k beta_floor^2 in the clock reading is bounded by k < 5e-9 at declared stabilities (ground optical clocks over a sidereal day; annual motion; GPS orbital motion weakest at 9e-6); zero is consistent; same order as the Ives-Stilwell type literature bound.
statements.author: Claude Code (proposal, 2026-10-30)
statements.decider: the declared stabilities (inputs, not measured here); a published clock-comparison analysis would tighten or fix the bound
statements.placement_note: attaches to the frame caveat (row 12); Appendix A II.3 preferred-frame tests
statements.outcome: HELD WITH ONE PREDICTION MISSED (sealed GPS-orbital bound off by a factor 1000; left standing)

statements.statement: The GPS eccentricity correction F e sqrt(A) sin E is the periodic part of the clock-in-motion law integrated along the orbit; F from the law matches the interface specification to 9e-11 relative; the constant part is the circular rate. One law, both GPS corrections.
statements.author: Claude Code (proposal, 2026-10-30)
statements.decider: met: F to 9e-11; amplitudes to 1e-4 ns
statements.placement_note: attaches to GPS (row 10) and the clock in motion (row 11)
